title: Virtual destructors
learningGoals: explain why a base destructor must be virtual
predict the output with and without virtual

youtube.title: C++ Virtual Destructors: Avoid This Bug | C++ Programming EP 66
youtube.description: In this episode you will explain why a base destructor must be virtual, predict the output with and without virtual and read the compiler warning, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Virtual destructors · 0:54 A virtual destructor · 1:34 What delete runs · 2:04 Second program · 3:04 Recap · 3:35 Bug of the Day · 4:23 Challenge · 4:43 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "VIRTUAL ~" in tomato on pastel blue; Xecxec next to a tilde wearing a crown; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a tilde wearing a crown

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we fix a classic bug. It hides in code that looks right, and it leaks memory.

scenes.onScreen: "Virtual destructors": numbered lines (1. Deleting through a base pointer needs a virtual destructor; 2. Without it, only the base part is destroyed; 3. Smart pointers need it too) and an analogy card: a cleaning crew: if the manager only knows the lobby, the back room is never cleaned
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: When you delete an object through a base pointer, the compiler must find the right destructor. If the base destructor is not virtual, only the base destructor runs. The derived part is never cleaned. The rule is simple. A class with any virtual function gets a virtual destructor. Think of a cleaning crew. If the manager only knows the lobby, the back room is never cleaned.
points: Deleting through a base pointer needs a virtual destructor
Without it, only the base part is destroyed

analogy.title: Virtual destructors
analogy.body: A cleaning crew: if the manager only knows the lobby, the back room is never cleaned

scenes.onScreen: vdtor.cpp: both destructors run, in the right order
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 6] The base destructor is virtual. [HL 11] The Dog destructor overrides it. [HL 15] The pointer is an Animal pointer, and the object is a Dog. [HL 16] Delete finds the real type. Dog gone prints first. Then Animal gone prints. Both parts are cleaned.

scenes.onScreen: a table: with and without a virtual destructor
scenes.animation: Table rows slide in one by one; the row the narrator mentions glows butter
scenes.narration: The table shows both cases. With a virtual destructor, delete runs the Dog destructor, and then the Animal one. Without virtual, only the Animal destructor runs. The result is undefined behaviour.

diagram.caption: a table: with and without a virtual destructor

scenes.onScreen: smart.cpp: unique_ptr needs the virtual destructor too
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 16] A smart pointer to Animal holds a Dog. [HL 17] The program prints working. [HL 18] At the end, the unique pointer deletes the object through the base type. Because the destructor is virtual, both Dog gone and Animal gone print. The rule is the same for smart pointers.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as smart dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints working, then Dog gone, then Animal gone.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. Deleting through a base pointer needs a virtual destructor. Two. Without it, only the base destructor runs. Three. A class with a virtual function needs a virtual destructor. Four. The same rule holds for smart pointers. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: Deleting through a base pointer needs a virtual destructor.
Without it, only the base destructor runs.
A class with a virtual function needs a virtual destructor.
The same rule holds for smart pointers.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: A base destructor that is not virtual
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; the g++ warning appears in tomato; the fix slides in and the warning goes away with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. The class has a virtual function, but the destructor is not virtual. The compiler warns that deleting an object of polymorphic class type might cause undefined behaviour. Only the Animal part would be destroyed. Make the destructor virtual.

scenes.onScreen: Why was the destructor so tired? It had to clean up after the whole family.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: Why was the destructor so tired? It had to clean up after the whole family.

scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Write a base class with one virtual function. Add a virtual destructor. Explain in a comment why it is needed. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: multiple inheritance and the diamond. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Compiler output (a warning, the program still builds):

vdtor.cpp: In function 'int main()':
vdtor.cpp:17:5: warning: deleting object of polymorphic class type 'Animal' which has non-virtual destructor might cause undefined behavior [-Wdelete-non-virtual-dtor]
   17 |     delete a;
      |     ^~~~~~~~
bug.why: Delete through a base pointer only runs the base destructor, when it is not virtual. The Dog part is never destroyed.

pun: "Why was the destructor so tired? It had to clean up after the whole family."
challenge: Write a base class with one virtual function. Add a virtual destructor. Explain in a comment why it is needed.
challengeAnswer: Delete through a base pointer needs the real destructor to run. A virtual destructor makes the compiler find it.
